title: VSpGEMM: Exploiting Versal ACAP for High-Performance SpGEMM Acceleration
problem: Sparse general matrix-matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is fundamental in deep learning and scientific computing, but sparse matrices require compact storage and produce irregular memory access patterns, creating communication and computation bottlenecks. Existing accelerators struggle with storage format overhead and intermediate product merging.
motivation: SpGEMM is pervasive in DNN and HPC workloads; CPU and GPU implementations incur high data movement overhead and irregular access penalties that specialized hardware can mitigate.
method: VSpGEMM is a specialized accelerator built on Xilinx Versal, a reconfigurable chip combining fixed math units called AI Engines with programmable logic. It introduces BCSX, a storage format that reorganizes sparse matrix data into regular block patterns for both row-major and column-major data layouts, eliminating the random memory access that normally slows sparse computation. The system uses multi-level tiling to decompose the problem into nested layers of chunks, each sized to fit in an AI Engine's local memory. It then partitions the work: AI Engines handle repetitive calculations efficiently, while programmable logic orchestrates combining intermediate results, which reduces data movement between components.
key_novelty: BCSX, a block-wise storage format that converts irregular sparse data into regular memory access patterns, enabling efficient hierarchical execution split between fixed and programmable hardware.
contributions: BCSX storage format enabling fixed-pattern memory access for sparse matrices
Multi-level tiling decomposition optimized for Versal AIE array hierarchy
Hybrid AIE/PL intermediate product merging reducing memory demand
2.65× speedup over prior SOTA GEMM on Versal; 33.62× energy efficiency vs. cuSPARSE on RTX 4090

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 33.62× energy efficiency vs cuSPARSE on RTX 4090

limitations: Performance on dynamic sparsity patterns and scalability to larger matrix sizes not discussed; Versal-specific optimizations limit portability.
primary_theme: high-performance SpGEMM acceleration on heterogeneous Versal ACAP via block-wise storage and hybrid dataflow
